newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA COMPLETE SIGNING OF COLLYMORE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA COMPLETE SIGNING OF COLLYMORE.

text.p: Aston Villa completed the signing of Liverpool and England striker Stan Collymore on Tuesday for a club record fee of seven million pounds ($11.4 million).
The deal takes the 26-year-old former Nottingaham Forest forward's total transfer fees over the last four years to 17.7 million pounds ($28.7 million).
Collymore, who cost liverpool a then British record 8.5 million pounds ($13.8 million) when he moved to Anfield in June 1995, signed a four-year contract with Villa with a further one year option.
"I used to support Villa as a boy so this is really a dream move home for me," said Collymore who lives only 30 minutes from Villa's training ground.
"I'm very excited at the prospect of playing alongside Dwight Yorke. We can be as big a threat in the premiership as I think my partnership with Robbie Fowler was at Liverpool."
He said he would always be grateful to Liverpool fans for their support.
"But not being able to command a regular place in the Liverpool side was very frustrating -- one of the main reasons I jumped at the chance of joining Villa," he said.
"I'm confident Villa will see the best of me over the next four years. If I do well enough here hopefully it could also help me get back in the England sqad."
Villa manager Brian Little, who made two failed previous attempts to sign Collymore during the season, said he was delighted to have landed him at last.

"We have established ourselves as a top six side in the premiership over the last two years and with Stan in the team I am optimistic we can now push on and challenge for the title and have a good crack at doing well in Europe.

"I don't envisage any problems handling Stan despite his reputation. I am looking forward to developing the sort of close relationship I have with all my players. He's a smashing lad and we will get on well together.
